# `overwritten-owning-value`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports assignment over an owning binding before its previous allocation is
released.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Replacing the only visible owner loses the address needed to release the
original allocation.

## When it fires

It applies to simple allocation bindings and optional owning values in retry
loops that are reassigned without an intervening matching cleanup. It also
applies to proven owned fields of stored container elements, including
assignments made through a direct element pointer alias, and to a method that
replaces a field its type's `deinit` frees.

A field replacement is not reported when the previous value holds no
allocation: in an `init` method, after an assignment on every path of `""`,
`undefined`, `null`, `&.{}`, `.{}` or `.empty`, after the old value is moved
elsewhere (`old.tree = self.tree`), or when a guarded first assignment is
followed by a release of the field on the function's other path. A type
without a `deinit` that frees the field leaves its release to the owner, often
an arena, and is not reported either.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn make(gpa: std.mem.Allocator) !void {
    var buf = try gpa.alloc(u8, 8);
    buf = try gpa.alloc(u8, 16);
    gpa.free(buf);
}
```
